correctness.rationale: With 10 vertices and a connected bridgeless graph, its graphic matroid has rank 9, no coloops, and a shellable 8-dimensional independence complex with all reduced homology in degree 8. For a permutation of graph edges with t cycles on an invariant k-edge forest, the oriented cellular action has sign (-1)^(k-t); multiplied by augmented degree sign (-1)^(k-1) this is (-1)^(t+1). Union-find forest tests exhaust all 32768 edge subsets, giving 22292 forests; orbit enumeration gives seven exact alternating sums (-240,0,0,0,0,0,0). Independent direct signed face-trace computations for all 120 permutations agree. Character theory of rational S5 representations identifies precisely two regular summands. Reproducibility is provided in self-contained verify.py; finite enumeration covers a finite domain, whereas the shellability input is a cited general theorem.

originality.rationale: The precise new claim is a complete, explicit rational S5-homology module for the Petersen graphic-matroid forest complex: two regular representations. The cited classical shellability/Tutte evaluation gives ordinary homological concentration but no group character; the general equivariant matroid paper provides related theory without enumerating this Petersen instance. A direct all-120-element signed trace computation checks the novel evaluation. Targeted literature and research-indexed comparisons found only scientifically different Petersen complexes (matching, cut, graph-Morse, configuration spaces). Residual risk: a broad formula may allow a comparable evaluation, and unindexed specific computations could exist.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical ten-vertex highly symmetric graph, and the forest complex is its natural graphic-matroid topological model. The 240-dimensional nonequivariant homology does not determine its symmetry structure. Exact uniform zero traces on all six nontrivial S5 conjugacy classes give an unexpectedly simple twice-regular module, explicit multiplicities of all seven Specht families, and a two-dimensional invariant space. This exact natural equivariant invariant is useful for comparison of homological representations of graphic matroids and is not a parameter-adjusted small improvement or routine reformulation; the calculation uses a nontrivial all-orbit cancellation.
